name: Developer verification
plain: Android checks that sideloaded apps come from a registered developer.
meaning: Adds identity checks for apps outside Google Play on certified devices in four markets from Sep 30, 2026; global rollout planned for 2027 and later.

android.permission: n/a (developer registration in Android Developer Console)
android.prompt_ui: Advanced flow: enable developer options and wait 24 hours
android.store_policy: Play and Console: registered developers only; ADB installs remain
android.note: Applies to Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand from Sep 30, 2026.

ios.store_policy: EU alternative distribution requires Apple notarization
ios.note: iOS notarizes apps outside the App Store in the EU.

limits.headline: Can only install on many Android phones if the developer is registered with Google
limits.user_action: You open an app file from outside the store and try to install it
can: Install apps from verified developers on certified Android phones
Use the advanced flow after turning on developer options and waiting 24 hours
Install outside the App Store on iPhone in the EU, after Apple's notarization check
cannot: Install from an unregistered developer in the starting countries without the advanced flow
Skip the check in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand from September 30, 2026
Install outside the App Store on iPhone outside the EU
limits.differs: Android adds developer checks from 2026 in four countries first. iPhone uses Apple notarization in the EU.

story.what_it_is: Android checks that apps installed from outside Google Play come from a registered developer.

marketing.name: Android developer verification
marketing.pitch: Google presents developer verification as a way to cut malware by tying sideloaded apps to a known developer.

story.for_you: You install an app from a website or another store and it may be blocked unless its maker is registered. Experienced users can follow a longer advanced path that includes a 24 hour wait.
story.for_makers: Makers outside Google Play must now register and prove who they are. Google says it cuts scams and malware, while critics worry it limits small and anonymous developers.

use_cases.example: Scammers push a fake bank app by link. Verification makes it harder to hide behind an anonymous developer.
A hobby game studio shares its game on its own site and must register as a developer first.
A student or hobbyist gets a lighter account type to install their own tests.
A company installs its own app on staff phones and registers the developer name.
A malware campaign that dropped repackaged apps is easier to trace to a real account.
A third party store lists apps and checks each developer is verified.
An open source tool installed by file needs its maker to be listed.

story.android_note: Starts in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand on Sep 30, 2026, with a wider rollout planned for 2027.
story.ios_note: iOS notarizes apps outside the App Store in the EU.

history.change: Developer verification live in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand on Sep 30, 2026
